subject: future
topic: Algorithmic curation is narrowing the range of human aesthetic preferences
angle: While algorithmic filtering is associated with decreased information diversity, these systems can also be designed to facilitate creative self-transformation and simultaneous gains in accuracy and diversity.
title: The Architecture of Taste

hooks.text: Is your taste being curated or created?
You think algorithms narrow your world. They might also be expanding it.
You are letting a system define your aesthetic boundaries.
A screen glows in a dark room.

reveal.headline: Algorithms can be designed to expand your taste.
reveal.body: While filtering often limits diversity, systems can be built to increase variety and support your creative growth.

explain.headline: The evidence on algorithmic curation is mixed.
explain.body: Current research shows that online content adaptation is often linked to a decrease in information diversity. However, specific designs can achieve simultaneous gains in accuracy and variety.

matters.headline: The design choice dictates your boundaries.
matters.body: That may be why your digital experience feels narrow. It is not just a byproduct of your habits, but a result of how the system is built to function.

example.headline: You scroll through a music app.
example.body: You listen to a new artist. You wonder if you would have found them alone or if the system led you there first.

question.headline: Who is choosing your next preference?

stat.label: simultaneous gains possible in new algorithms

claims.text: Recommendation systems can facilitate both algorithmic control and creative self-transformation.
claims.quote: Thus, recommendation systems can facilitate both algorithmic control and creative self-transformation, which calls for a theorization of this new cultural medium as a space of tension.

claims.text: Users on the music recommendation website last.fm use recommender systems to examine and transform their own music taste.
claims.quote: User practices on the music recommendation website last.fm reveal that many users do not only utilize the website to receive guidance about music products but also to examine and transform an aspect of their self, i.e. their ‘music taste’.

claims.text: A new algorithm can obtain simultaneous gains in both accuracy and diversity of recommendations without relying on any semantic or context-specific information.
claims.quote: By tuning the hybrid appropriately we are able to obtain, without relying on any semantic or context-specific information, simultaneous gains in both accuracy and diversity of recommendations.

claims.text: A recommendation algorithm considering both the effects of similar and dissimilar users performs better than standard collaborative filtering for both accuracy and diversity.
claims.quote: Extensive analyses on three datasets, namely MovieLens, Netflix and Amazon, show that our method performs much better than the standard collaborative filtering algorithm for both accuracy and diversity.

claims.text: Algorithmic filtering and adaptation of online content to personal preferences is often associated with a decrease in the diversity of information to which users are exposed.
claims.quote: The algorithmic filtering and adaption of online content to personal preferences and interests is often associated with a decrease in the diversity of information to which users are exposed.

verdict: The evidence shows that while algorithms can narrow information exposure, they are also capable of being designed to increase diversity and support user self-cultivation.
caveat: The sources do not provide a definitive causal link between algorithmic curation and the narrowing of human aesthetic preferences, as some studies focus on design possibilities rather than outcomes.
caption:
Algorithms shape what you see, hear, and feel.

Research shows that while these systems often decrease information diversity, they can also be designed to facilitate creative self-transformation. However, the evidence is mixed and does not prove a definitive causal link between curation and narrowed preferences.
